topic.title: Why is Lesotho completely surrounded by South Africa?
topic.map_answer: the border itself: the Basotho held the high mountains while Boer settlers took the lowland valleys around them, so the line drawn on the Caledon River and the mountain edge left Lesotho as an island of high ground inside South Africa

title: Why does South Africa have a hole in it?
description:
Lesotho is a whole country. So why does it sit in the middle of South Africa?
A mountain fortress, a border pushed back war by war and one call to Britain, on the map.
Sources: Wikipedia (Jan 2024). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Mountains or the British: which really saved Lesotho? Comment

lines.text: Why does South Africa have a hole in the middle?
That hole is a country, Lesotho.
A whole kingdom of 30,355 km², about as big as Belgium, and every road out of it crosses into South Africa.
It began with a chief called Moshoeshoe, who led his people up Thaba Bosiu, a flat-topped mountain no army could take.
From that fortress he gathered clans scattered by war into one nation, the Basotho, farming the wide valleys to the west.
But who else wanted those valleys? Boer settlers, who rolled in by ox wagon and founded the Orange Free State right on top of them.
War after war, the Boers took the farmland, and the Basotho were pushed back toward the mountains.
So how did any of it survive? Moshoeshoe asked Britain to protect what was left, and his land became Basutoland.
Then a treaty drew its north-west border down the Caledon River, where it still runs today.
Decades later, the British colonies all around it joined into one country, South Africa. Basutoland stayed out.
In the end it became the independent Kingdom of Lesotho, a country of mountains with South Africa on every side.
And the Basotho kept only the high ground: the lowest point in Lesotho is 1,400 m above the sea, higher than any other country's lowest point.
Mountains or the British: which really saved it? Tell me. And next time someone asks you,

At 50.0 s the whole union turns that blue and South Africa's map flag sits over Basutoland's west half, with no BASUTOLAND label or edge yet: the edge and label start at 'stayed' (~50 s) with under 1 s left in the beat while the camera is still moving. Fix: give Basutoland a contrasting fill (or leave it uncoloured) from 'colonies' on, keep the SA flag off it (place it west, near 24E), and bring in the edge and label at 'joined', so the hole stays visible while the colours merge.
